To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the expression of miRNAs in plasma and tumor tissue of breast cancer patients is altered compared to healthy women; 2) plasma miRNAs are associated with breast cancer subtypes and with clinical parameters; 3) plasma miRN-10a, -21, -210, -373, -378, -486, and -654 are associated with survival of patients with breast cancer; and 4) plasma miR-21 and -210 are associated with recurrence of
VEGF and ANG-2 levels are elevated in the postoperative period after breast cancer surgery, and that ANG-2 is associated with postoperative complications.

the expression of the genes of the vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGFs) and their receptors (VEGFRs) and the genes of the angiopoietin family and their receptor (Tie-2) were upregulated in the breast cancer tissue, compared to normal breast tissues, and that the expression of VEGF, Ang1, and Tie-2 were upregulated in plasma of patients with breast cancer compared with normal controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of angiopoietins and their receptors, and VEGF in the development of metastasis and the role of angiogenesis in the development of the disease.
the development and application of novel methods of analysis for the determination of the concentration of trace amounts of organic compounds in biological materials.

the study of the mechanisms of action of the angiogenesis factors, vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGFs) and their receptors, and of the angiopoietins and their receptors, with particular reference to their role in tumour angiogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no evidence that VEGF, Ang-1 and Ang-2 are useful as biomarkers for the prediction or prognosis of response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy or for the prediction or prognostic value for recurrence or survival of breast cancer.
the evidence does not suggest a role for any specific dietary supplement in the management of breast cancer.
the results of the studies on the association of the VEGF, Ang1, and Ang2 with breast cancer are inconclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that VEGF and its receptors are upregulated after breast cancer surgery and that angiopoietins and their receptors are downregulated.
we found that surgery for breast cancer causes an acute increase in VEGF, Ang-1, Ang-2, Tie2, and a decrease in Tie1.
the results of this study suggest that the angiogenic factors and their receptors may play an important role in the post-operative changes in breast cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of VEGF and its receptors as biomarkers in breast cancer may not be as straightforward as previously assumed.
there are many factors that contribute to the development of breast cancer, including lifestyle and genetics, and that it is not just one single thing that causes it.
we can use the same methods that have been used for years to study the effects of surgery on breast cancer cells to study the effect of surgery on the immune system.
